verdict.rationale: First-party docs show Facial Similarity reports comparing a live photo, live video or motion capture against the face on the applicant's most recent identity document. The Motion variant assesses liveness through head-turn or randomized head-movement challenges. However, the evidence never documents specific defenses against printed photos, screen replays or replayed video. missing for 10: documented presentation-attack defenses against printed photos, screens and replayed video; independent or hands-on corroboration of liveness accuracy.

support.subject: As a risk analyst, selfie checks match the live user to the document portrait with liveness detection — documented defenses against printed photos, screens, and replayed video

citations.quote: Facial Similarity reports compare the most recent live photo, live video or motion capture provided by an applicant during an identity verification flow to the face on their most recently captured identity document
Motion also assesses liveness by asking users to complete either a simple head turn pattern in both directions or four randomized head movements.
A Facial Similarity report compares a selfie or video provided by an applicant to the photo in the most recent identity document they have provided.
